slides.title: Letters make sounds
slides.text:
Each word is made of **sounds**. Letters show those sounds.

Say a word slowly: **c-a-t**. Three sounds, three letters.

slides.title: The silent e
slides.text:
An **e** at the end is often silent. It makes the vowel **say its name**.

cap → **cape**
kit → **kite**
hop → **hope**

slides.title: Two letters, one sound
slides.text:
Some letter pairs make **one** sound.

**sh** as in ship
**ch** as in chair
**th** as in three

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
To find a spelling mistake:

1. Read each word slowly.
2. Say the sounds you hear.
3. Check: do the letters match the sounds?

Point to the sentence with the word that does not match.

sentences.t: He likes to ride his bike.

example.explain: In **bike**, the silent **e** makes the **i** say its name. Without the e, it would be **bik**, which is not a word.

together.passage: Mona has a new bik. It is red. She rides it to the park. Her dad walks with her.
together.hint: Say each word. Which one has a vowel that says its name but no silent e?
together.good: Yes! It should be **bike**. The silent e makes the i say its name.

sentences: She rides it to the park.
evidence.stem: The answer was: bik should be bike. Tap the sentence with that word.
evidence.wrong: All the words here are spelled right. Find the sentence with bik.

checks.passage: Tom has a kite. He flies it on the hill. The wind is strong.
checks.stem: Which word has the long i sound, like in "time"?
checks.why: **kite** has a silent e, so the i says its name, like in time.

checks.passage: We went to the beach. I found a shell. It was white.
checks.stem: Which word starts with the same sound as "ship"?
checks.why: **shell** starts with **sh**, the same sound as ship.

checks.passage: It is my birthday. Dad cut the cak. We all ate some.
checks.why: It should be **cake**. The silent e makes the a say its name.

again.title: Say it, then spell it
again.text:
1. Say the word **slowly**.
2. Tap one finger for each sound.
3. Write a letter or letter pair for each sound.
4. Long vowel at the end? Try a silent **e**.
again.example: **hope**: h - o - p. The o says its name, so add a silent e: **hope**.

slides.title: One sound, many spellings
slides.text:
The same sound can be spelled in different ways.

Long **a**: r**ai**n, d**ay**, c**a**k**e**
Long **e**: tr**ee**, p**ea**ch
Long **o**: b**oa**t, sn**ow**, h**o**m**e**

slides.title: Vowel teams
slides.text:
Two vowels together often make one long sound.

**ai** is usually in the **middle** of a word: rain, paint.
**ay** is usually at the **end**: day, play.

slides.title: After a short vowel
slides.text:
After a short vowel, the /k/ sound at the end is often **ck**.

ro**ck**  ba**ck**  du**ck**

After a long vowel team, it is often just **k**: b**oo**k, s**ee**k.

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
To prove a spelling is wrong:

1. Find the word that looks strange.
2. Name the sound pattern it should follow (for example **ai** in the middle).
3. Point to the sentence where the word appears.

sentences.t: The sky was grey all day.
Then the rain began to fall.

example.explain: **rain** has the long a sound in the **middle** of the word, so it uses **ai**. **day** and **stayed** use **ay**.

together.passage: Last weekend it began to rane. Fahad stayed inside and read a book about boats. His sister made tea for the whole family. When the clouds went away, they walked down the road to see the puddles.
together.hint: Look for a long a sound in the middle of a word. Which pattern should it use?
together.good: Yes! It should be **rain**. A long a in the middle of a word is often spelled **ai**.

sentences: Last weekend it began to rane.
Fahad stayed inside and read a book about boats.
His sister made tea for the whole family.
When the clouds went away, they walked down the road to see the puddles.
evidence.stem: The answer was: rane should be rain. Tap the sentence with that word.
evidence.wrong: Every word in this sentence is spelled correctly. Find the sentence with rane.

checks.passage: Aisha sat in the shade. She ate a peach. Then she wrote in her notebook.
checks.stem: Which word has the same vowel sound as "green"?
checks.why: **peach** has the long e sound, spelled **ea**. Green spells the same sound **ee**.

checks.passage: The goat stood on a big rok. It ate the green leaves. Then it jumped down.
checks.why: It should be **rock**. After a short vowel, the /k/ sound at the end is spelled **ck**.

checks.passage: Yusuf put on his coat. He took his bag and his phone. He was ready to go.
checks.stem: Which word spells the long o sound with "oa"?
checks.why: **coat** uses the vowel team **oa**. Phone and go also have long o, but spelled differently.

again.title: Where is the sound?
again.text:
For long a, ask **where** you hear it.

In the **middle**? Try **ai**: tr**ai**n.
At the **end**? Try **ay**: pl**ay**.
again.example:
"We will p_ _ nt the wall today."

The long a is in the middle of **paint**, so it is **ai**. In **today** it is at the end, so it is **ay**.

slides.title: Silent letters
slides.text:
Some letters are written but **not heard**.

**kn**ot, **kn**ee (k is silent)
**wr**ite, **wr**ong (w is silent)
la**mb**, cli**mb** (b is silent)

slides.title: Letters that change sound
slides.text:
**c** sounds like **s** before e, i or y: **c**ity, **c**entre.
**g** often sounds like **j** before e, i or y: **g**iant, **g**ym.

**ph** sounds like **f**: **ph**oto.
**igh** says long i: n**igh**t, l**igh**t.

slides.title: Word endings
slides.text:
The ending **-tion** sounds like "shun".

na**tion**  sta**tion**  celebra**tion**

If you hear "shun" at the end of a long word, **-tion** is the most common spelling.

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
To find the misspelled word:

1. Check words with tricky patterns: silent letters, ph, igh, -tion.
2. Ask: does this word follow its pattern?
3. Point to the sentence with the word that breaks it.

Careful: a word that **looks** odd may be correct, like **lamb** or **write**.

sentences.t: The knight climbed the castle wall.

example.explain: **knight** has a silent **k** and the **igh** pattern. **climbed** has a silent **b**. They look strange, but they are correct.

together.passage: Every nite, Huda writes in her diary. Last week she wrote about an old photograph of her grandmother as a young girl. In the picture, her grandmother is standing next to a tall palm tree. She is holding a small white lamb in her arms.
together.hint: Some words look odd but are correct. Which one should use the igh pattern?
together.good: Yes! It should be **night**. The long i sound here is spelled **igh**.

sentences: Every nite, Huda writes in her diary.
Last week she wrote about an old photograph of her grandmother as a young girl.
In the picture, her grandmother is standing next to a tall palm tree.
She is holding a small white lamb in her arms.
evidence.stem: The answer was: nite should be night. Tap the sentence with that word.
evidence.wrong: The tricky words in this sentence are spelled correctly. Find the sentence with nite.

checks.passage: On our class trip, we walked through the old city. We saw a cactus garden, a copper pot shop and a coin museum.
checks.stem: In which word does the letter c sound like s?
checks.why: In **city**, c comes before i, so it sounds like s. In the others, c comes before a or o and sounds like k.

checks.passage: Salma tied a knot in the string. Then she pulled hard. The tent stood up.
checks.stem: Which word has a silent letter?
checks.why: In **knot**, the k is written but not heard.

checks.passage: Our school had a big celebrasion for National Day. Students sang songs and waved green flags.
checks.why: It should be **celebration**. The "shun" sound at the end is spelled **-tion**.

again.title: Make a pattern list
again.text:
Keep a short list of tricky patterns:

**kn, wr, mb** = silent letters
**ph** = f
**igh** = long i
**-tion** = shun

When a word looks wrong, check it against your list.
again.example:
"The ligt was bright."

**bright** uses igh, so **ligt** should be **light**.

slides.title: Same sound, different letters
slides.text:
The **sh** sound has many spellings in longer words.

**ti**: na**ti**on
**ci**: spe**ci**al, musi**ci**an
**ssi**: mi**ssi**on
**ch**: ma**ch**ine

slides.title: Clues from the word
slides.text:
The spelling often follows the **base word**.

music → musi**ci**an (the c stays)
express → expre**ssi**on (the ss stays)
decide → deci**si**on

Think of the base word to choose the letters.

slides.title: More patterns
slides.text:
**ch** can say /k/ in words from Greek: **ch**emistry, **ch**orus.

After a short vowel, /j/ is often **dge**: bri**dge**, e**dge**.
After a long vowel or a consonant, it is **ge**: ca**ge**, hu**ge**, cha**nge**.

proof.title: Prove it from the text
proof.text:
To analyse a word's spelling:

1. Say the word and find the sound you are asked about.
2. Look at the **exact letters** that spell that sound.
3. Use the base word or the vowel before it to check the pattern.

Point to the sentence where the word appears.

example.explain: In **musician**, the sh sound is spelled **ci** because the base word is **music**. The c from music stays in the new word.

together.passage: The science club planned a special experiment for the open day. Each member had a different mission for the day. Latifa had to measure the temperature of the water, and Reem was in charge of the stopwatch. Their teacher reminded them that a good scientist checks every calculation twice. In the end, the experiment was a success, and visitors asked many questions.
together.stem: In which word is the sh sound spelled with the letters "ci"?
together.hint: Find the sh sound in each word, then look at the exact letters that spell it.
together.good: Yes! In **special**, the sh sound is spelled **ci**. Mission uses ssi and calculation uses ti.

sentences: The science club planned a special experiment for the open day.
Each member had a different mission for the day.
Latifa had to measure the temperature of the water, and Reem was in charge of the stopwatch.
Their teacher reminded them that a good scientist checks every calculation twice.
In the end, the experiment was a success, and visitors asked many questions.
evidence.stem: The answer was: special. Tap the sentence with that word.
evidence.wrong: This sentence does not have the word with ci. Look for special.

checks.passage: My brother studies chemistry at university. Each morning he checks his notes on the bus. He says the chapter on gases is the hardest.
checks.stem: In which word does "ch" sound like k?
checks.why: In **chemistry**, ch sounds like k. In the other words, ch has its usual sound.

checks.passage: We crossed the old brige at dawn. The edge of the river was covered in mist. A large cage of pigeons sat near the gate.
checks.why: It should be **bridge**. After a short vowel, the j sound is spelled **dge**, like in edge.

checks.passage: Grandfather lives in an old house near the train station. He reads fiction in the evening and rarely watches television.
checks.stem: Which word ends with the same sound as "vision"?
checks.why: **Vision** and **television** both end in a soft "zhun" sound spelled **-sion**. Station and fiction end in "shun".

again.title: Start from the base word
again.text:
For a long word, find the **smaller word** inside it.

The smaller word often keeps its letters in the long word.
again.example:
electric → electri**ci**an (keeps the c)
confess → confe**ssi**on (keeps the ss)

So it is not "electrishan": the base word tells you to use **ci**.
